info.title: OpenMettle application API
info.summary: Versioned application contract for capabilities, projects, conversations, artifacts and durable run replay.
info.description: Canonical source for the OpenMettle v1 application API contract. Wire rules, compatibility policy and limits are recorded in docs/adr/0007-application-api-contract.md; authorization and project lifecycle in docs/adr/0027-authorization-and-private-projects.md. Every operation carries x-openmettle-implementation: `implemented` operations are served by an API started with OPENMETTLE_API_AUTH_CONFIG, and `not-implemented` operations are not served. An API started without OPENMETTLE_API_AUTH_CONFIG serves no operation; without OPENMETTLE_API_ARTIFACTS_DIR the artifact upload and download operations answer 503 provisioning. Artifact storage is described in docs/adr/0031-filesystem-artifact-storage-and-streaming-multipart.md. Fixtures under contracts/fixtures are generated from the examples in this document by scripts/contract_fixtures.py. ADR 0036 defines managed conversation history, catalog and durable submission. Configure catalog_file and admission_limits in the version-2 auth document. Run mutations require cursor_keys. A full queue returns Retry-After in seconds.

post.description: Creates an artifact and its revision 1 in the caller's personal scope or a project scope. The artifact is private to the caller until shared. The target is authorized on the primary before anything is reserved or written. The Idempotency-Key is scoped to the caller, the operation and its target: an exact retry, even with another multipart boundary or part order, returns the same revision with 201 and is charged once. The same key with another file, media type, file name or max_bytes fails with idempotency_conflict, as does a key whose earlier upload failed; a retry while that key's upload is still streaming fails with conflict. Storage quota exhaustion is quota; unconfigured storage limits or an API without OPENMETTLE_API_ARTIFACTS_DIR are provisioning. A malformed or truncated body, a file over max_bytes and a refused metadata part are validation. An upload must finish within 600 seconds.

requestBody.description: The file and its metadata, streamed: the server never buffers the whole file and enforces max_bytes on the bytes it observes, whatever Content-Length says.

fileFirst.summary: An upload with the file part first
fileFirst.description: Sent with Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=openmettle-example-a. Settles as the ArtifactRevisionActive example; the part's media type is stored as text/plain;charset=utf-8.
fileFirst.serializedValue:
--openmettle-example-a
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="notes.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

hello, world
--openmettle-example-a
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="metadata"
Content-Type: application/json

{}
--openmettle-example-a--

metadataFirst.summary: The same upload with another boundary and the metadata part first
metadataFirst.description: Sent with Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=openmettle-example-retry. Under the same Idempotency-Key this is an exact retry of ArtifactUploadFileFirst: it returns the same revision and is charged once.
metadataFirst.serializedValue:
--openmettle-example-retry
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="metadata"
Content-Type: application/json

{}
--openmettle-example-retry
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="notes.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

hello, world
--openmettle-example-retry--

get.summary: Read the caller's access to one artifact
get.description: A artifact is private to its creator until shared. A project owner, an account administrator or another member cannot read an unshared item: it is not_found, as is an item in a deleted project or one whose project membership the caller has lost. In an archived project the item stays readable with access read.

200.description: The caller's access to the artifact.

post.summary: Upload the next revision of an artifact
post.description: Appends the next immutable revision. The caller needs write access to the artifact: an item the caller may not read is not_found, a reader gets policy and an artifact in an archived project gets conflict. The target is authorized on the primary before anything is reserved or written. The Idempotency-Key is scoped to the caller, the operation and its target: an exact retry, even with another multipart boundary or part order, returns the same revision with 201 and is charged once. The same key with another file, media type, file name or max_bytes fails with idempotency_conflict, as does a key whose earlier upload failed; a retry while that key's upload is still streaming fails with conflict. Storage quota exhaustion is quota; unconfigured storage limits or an API without OPENMETTLE_API_ARTIFACTS_DIR are provisioning. A malformed or truncated body, a file over max_bytes and a refused metadata part are validation. An upload must finish within 600 seconds.

requestBody.description: The file and its metadata, streamed: the server never buffers the whole file and enforces max_bytes on the bytes it observes, whatever Content-Length says.

get.description: Needs current read access to the artifact, decided on the primary on every request. Works without OPENMETTLE_API_ARTIFACTS_DIR. A revision of another artifact is not_found.

Needs current read access to the artifact, decided on the primary on every request, so a revoked share, membership or approval stops the next download. Streams the bytes without buffering the file. Only an active revision serves content; another state is conflict. HEAD returns the same status and headers without a body. A stored file that is missing or has another size is internal. Without OPENMETTLE_API_ARTIFACTS_DIR the operation is provisioning.

schema.description: The content bytes, served with the revision's media_type as Content-Type.
The content bytes, served with the revision's media_type as Content-Type.

put.summary: Share a artifact with a user, group or the whole project
put.description: The creator holding editor or owner, or a project owner who can see the item, may share it. A viewer or another editor fails with policy. Inside a project the grantee must hold active project membership; the whole-project grantee is valid only in a project. New shares fail with conflict in an archived project.

post.summary: Revoke a share of a artifact
post.description: The same share managers as sharing, including in an archived project. The grantee need not remain a member, so stale shares can always be retired. The grantee loses access on its next request.

get.summary: List capabilities visible to the authenticated caller
get.description: Returns installed, authorization and readiness dimensions independently for each capability. Absence of an optional provider never makes the core unavailable, and this operation is not an input to the operational /readyz probe. The response never contains provider endpoints, credentials, model secrets or another user's inventory. The caller's principal is hydrated on the primary for each request; a disabled account, withdrawn approval or logged-out session fails with unauthenticated. This core-only installation returns an empty list.

get.summary: Read the caller's access to one conversation
get.description: A conversation is private to its creator until shared. A project owner, an account administrator or another member cannot read an unshared item: it is not_found, as is an item in a deleted project or one whose project membership the caller has lost. In an archived project the item stays readable with access read.

200.description: The caller's access to the conversation.

put.summary: Share a conversation with a user, group or the whole project
put.description: The creator holding editor or owner, or a project owner who can see the item, may share it. A viewer or another editor fails with policy. Inside a project the grantee must hold active project membership; the whole-project grantee is valid only in a project. New shares fail with conflict in an archived project.

post.summary: Revoke a share of a conversation
post.description: The same share managers as sharing, including in an archived project. The grantee need not remain a member, so stale shares can always be retired. The grantee loses access on its next request.

post.summary: Create a project owned by the caller
post.description: Any active caller may create a project. The caller becomes its only direct owner. Replaying the same Idempotency-Key with the identical body returns the project again.

get.summary: Read a project the caller is a member of
get.description: Any member may read the project's settings and their own effective role. A non-member, including an account administrator, receives not_found. A deleted project is not_found. An archived project stays readable; its settings, role grants and new shares fail with conflict until it is restored.

put.summary: Replace a project's name, instructions and defaults
put.description: Owner only. Replacing settings with identical values fails with conflict. A deleted project is not_found. An archived project stays readable; its settings, role grants and new shares fail with conflict until it is restored.

delete.description: Owner only, including while archived. Every live run in the project is cancelled. The project is then not_found for every operation, except that replaying the delete with the same Idempotency-Key again returns 204.

post.description: Owner only. Every live run in the project is cancelled. The project stays readable; settings, role grants and new shares fail with conflict until it is restored, while revocations, restore and delete stay available. Archiving an archived project fails with conflict.

put.summary: Give a user or group exactly one direct project role
put.description: Owner only. Demoting or removing the last direct user owner fails with policy. A user or local group must exist and be enabled. A deleted project is not_found. An archived project stays readable; its settings, role grants and new shares fail with conflict until it is restored.

post.summary: Revoke every direct project role of a user or group
post.description: Owner only, including while archived. Removing the last direct user owner fails with policy. Directory-mapped membership is unchanged. The removed member loses access to the project's items on its next request.
Owner only. No cancelled run is revived. Restoring a project that is not archived fails with conflict.

get.description: Read state, sequence and terminal event together. Conversation read access is required. Without cursor_keys this operation returns 503 provisioning.

200.description: Current run state and resume cursor.

get.summary: Replay and follow ordered run events
get.description: Events are retained for the life of the run. No cursor replays from the beginning. On invalid_cursor discard derived state, fetch the snapshot and resume with its cursor. The stream ends after terminal delivery or loss of access. Without cursor_keys this operation returns 503 provisioning.

200.description: Ordered visible events after the selected cursor.

204.description: The cursor is at the last sequence of a terminal run. Stop reconnecting.

post.description: Uses the admission resolver without writing. Counts include instructions, turn and part framing, attachments and qualified reasoning replay. A versioned catalog profile may declare prompt_bound with fixed_tokens, tokens_per_turn, tokens_per_part, tokens_per_byte and a nullable tokens_per_attachment for its estimator_revision. These deployment-qualified upper bounds apply to that profile. Missing evidence leaves the prompt count unknown.

post.description: The v2 auth settings accept an optional catalog_file (absolute path, at most 1 MiB) and admission_limits with live_per_actor, live_per_scope, queued_in_instance, queue_timeout_seconds and round_cap. All five limits are required together. A configured cursor key signs the returned snapshot. An exact retry uses its pinned input and configuration after reauthorization. A live limit yields 429. A full queue yields 503 with Retry-After. Admission binds the validated session to the run. YOLO requires an explicit runs.use_yolo grant. An exact replay from another active session preserves the original binding.

202.description: Cancellation requested from the lease holder.

get.summary: List the actionable approval for the run actor
get.description: The run actor needs current scope and conversation read access. Browser writes require the configured Origin. Return at most one current, undecided request while its binding, deadline, originating session and reviewed display policy are valid. A visible run with no actionable request returns an empty array.

post.summary: Record or replay an approval decision
post.description: The run actor needs current scope and conversation read access. Browser writes require the configured Origin. A new decision requires current execution authority and a live originating session. Exact key and input replay the original receipt after logout, archive or settlement. A changed input under the same key returns idempotency_conflict. A stale binding, another key after decision, or an invalid wait returns conflict.

browserSession.name: __Host-openmettle-session
browserSession.description: OpenMettle browser session (ADRs 0013 and 0019): the opaque credential in the Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, host-only cookie set by the browser sign-in callback. An unsafe method requires exactly one Origin header equal to the configured application origin; a safe method may omit Origin, but any Origin it sends must be that origin. A refused Origin is 401 unauthenticated. The cookie must occur once and never together with an Authorization header.

nativeSession.description: OpenMettle native session (ADRs 0023 and 0029): the opaque bearer credential returned by the native token endpoint after the system-browser code/PKCE handoff, sent as one `Authorization: Bearer` field and never together with the session cookie. Upstream OIDC provider tokens are never accepted as OpenMettle API credentials.

ApiVersion.description: Major.minor contract version of the response. The major always matches the /v1 path prefix. Consumers reject a major they do not support and accept any newer minor.

RetryAfter.description: Delay in seconds before a retry may succeed. Advisory; absence does not imply that a retry is safe or useful.

ContentLength.description: Exact number of bytes in this response body.

ContentRange.description: bytes first-last/total for a partial response; bytes */total when the range is not satisfiable.

ContentDisposition.description: attachment, with the display name as an RFC 8187 filename* parameter when the revision has one. Every byte outside attr-char is percent-encoded.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque page cursor returned as next_cursor. A cursor is valid only for the same caller, operation, filters and sort order that produced it. Malformed, foreign, expired or tampered cursors fail with invalid_cursor.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. The server may return fewer.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-chosen key for a state-changing request. The server scopes it to the authenticated actor, the operation and its path target; any actor or user identity in the request body is never used for this purpose. Repeating the same key with the identical request returns the original outcome; the same key with a different request fails with idempotency_conflict. Retries after an uncertain outcome must resend the identical request, including any client-supplied input identity. No retention period or exactly-once execution is promised.

LastEventId.name: Last-Event-ID
LastEventId.description: Resume after the last event received by EventSource. Last-Event-ID takes precedence over after. Each may appear once. An unused after must still be a well-formed run cursor. Only the selected cursor is authenticated.

After.name: after
After.description: Resume after this opaque cursor when opening a stream. Last-Event-ID takes precedence over after. Each may appear once. An unused after must still be a well-formed run cursor. Only the selected cursor is authenticated.

ProjectId.name: project_id
ProjectId.description: The project's identifier. A malformed identifier fails with validation; a project the caller may not know about fails with not_found.

ConversationId.name: conversation_id
ConversationId.description: The conversation's identifier. A malformed identifier fails with validation; a conversation the caller may not know about fails with not_found.

ArtifactId.name: artifact_id
ArtifactId.description: The artifact's identifier. A malformed identifier fails with validation; a artifact the caller may not know about fails with not_found.

RevisionId.name: revision_id
RevisionId.description: The revision's identifier. A malformed identifier fails with validation; a revision of another artifact, or of an artifact the caller may not know about, fails with not_found.

ScopeId.name: scope_id
ScopeId.description: The scope of the new artifact: the caller's personal scope (the default when absent) or a project scope where the caller is an editor or owner. A missing, deleted or invisible project fails with not_found; a viewer gets policy; an archived project gets conflict.

MaxBytes.name: max_bytes
MaxBytes.description: The file's byte ceiling as a canonical decimal, 67108864 (64 MiB) by default. It is charged against storage quotas until the upload settles, then the actual size is charged instead. It is part of the request identity, so a retry must send the same value.

Range.name: Range
Range.description: One RFC 9110 byte range: bytes=first-last, bytes=first- or bytes=-suffix. A list of ranges, another unit or a malformed range fails with validation; a range that does not overlap the content fails with 416. With If-Range the whole content is sent, because no validator is issued.

RunId.name: run_id
RunId.description: Canonical run UUID. A missing run or a run in an unreadable conversation returns not_found.

ConversationScope.name: scope_id
ConversationScope.description: Return visible conversations in this scope. Defaults to the caller’s personal scope.

ApprovalId.name: approval_id
ApprovalId.description: Canonical approval UUID within this run.

lifecycle.summary: Heartbeat, creation, start and terminal cancellation

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or violates the contract (validation or invalid_cursor).

Unauthenticated.description: No valid OpenMettle application session was presented.

TooManyRequests.description: A quota or rate limit refused the request.

Internal.description: An unexpected server failure. No internal detail is disclosed.

Unavailable.description: A required service is unavailable or the account or deployment is not provisioned for the request.

Forbidden.description: The caller may know the target exists but may not perform the action (policy).

NotFound.description: The target does not exist, was deleted, or the caller may not know it exists (not_found).

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with current state, for example an unchanged value or an archived project (conflict), or reuses an Idempotency-Key for a different request (idempotency_conflict).

Timeout.description: A required service did not answer in time (timeout). The outcome of a write is unknown: retry with the identical request and Idempotency-Key.

RangeNotSatisfiable.description: The range does not overlap the content (range_not_satisfiable), including any range of an empty file.

ApiVersion.description: Major.minor contract version. This document defines major 1.

Uuid.description: Canonical lowercase UUID. Identifiers are random and never derived from secrets, digests or request content.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp with exactly six fractional digits and a Z offset.

NonNegativeDecimal.description: Canonical base-10 integer from 0 to 9223372036854775807 (signed 64-bit maximum) encoded as a string, without sign, leading zeros, exponent or fraction. Used for byte sizes and counters so JavaScript and Dart consumers cannot silently lose precision.

PositiveSequence.description: Canonical base-10 integer from 1 to 9223372036854775807 encoded as a string. Per-run event sequences start at 1.

IdempotencyKey.description: 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters (0x21-0x7E). Character and byte length are therefore equal.

Cursor.description: Opaque server-issued cursor in unpadded base64url characters. Store it unchanged. A run cursor authenticates the sequence, operation, run, scope and caller.

Code.description: Stable machine-readable code from an open vocabulary. Consumers must tolerate values they do not recognize.

PageInfo.description: Pagination state for list responses. next_cursor is null on the final page.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. detail is a bounded, safe message: it never contains credentials, upstream provider bodies, identity claims, internal identifiers or information about other users' resources. A resource the caller may not know about yields not_found rather than policy. Known codes are bound to their HTTP status; unrecognized codes are classified by status.

type.description: Problem type URI reference. v1 emits about:blank and relies on code for classification.

errors.description: Request locations that failed validation. Values supplied by the client are never echoed.

in.description: Request part: body, query, header or path (open vocabulary).

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the body, or /name for a parameter.

CapabilityList.description: Capabilities visible to the authenticated caller. An empty list is valid: the core has no optional provider installed.

Capability.description: One capability with independent dimensions. installed reports deployment configuration. authorization reports whether the caller may use it: true, false or null when not yet determined; null is unknown, never false. readiness reports provider observation and is present only when installed. No dimension implies another.

Readiness.description: Provider readiness. Known states are ready, degraded, unavailable and unknown (open vocabulary). ready, degraded and unavailable are observations and carry observed_at. unknown means no current observation; it is not unavailable and not ready. Consumers treat unrecognized states as not ready.

RunEventItem.description: One parsed text/event-stream item of the RunEventStream media type (OAS 3.2 sequential media type with itemSchema). id is the opaque resume cursor. data carries one JSON RunEvent; contentSchema is not validated automatically by OAS tooling, so consumers decode and validate it explicitly. Clients ignore event types they do not recognize but still advance their cursor to the item id. Comments and unknown SSE fields are discarded by SSE parsing before this schema applies.

RunEvent.description: Persisted event in ascending per-run sequence. Consumers advance past unknown types and versions and tolerate unknown reason codes. Version 1 run.failed reasons include queue_expired, approval_expired and invalid_wait.

ProjectName.description: 1 to 256 bytes, no leading or trailing whitespace and no control character.

ProjectDefaults.description: Project defaults: a JSON object of at most 16 KiB in compact form. The legacy top-level members folder_id, folder_ids, collection_id and collection_ids are refused.

AuditReason.description: Optional reason recorded in the append-only authorization audit. Defaults to the operationId.

Project.description: A project as the caller may read it. A project created before settings existed has an empty name, empty instructions and {} defaults at revision 0.

archived.description: An archived project stays readable; settings, role grants and new shares fail with conflict until it is restored.

role.description: The caller's effective role: the highest of its direct, local-group and OIDC-group grants. Open vocabulary.

MemberGrantee.description: A project member: a user, a local group or an OIDC group.

grantee_id.description: A user or local group UUID, or an exact OIDC group claim value of 1 to 1024 bytes without control characters.

ShareGrantee.description: A share recipient: a user, a local group, an OIDC group, or every member of the containing project (`project`, without grantee_id; project scopes only).

grantee_id.description: A user or local group UUID, or an exact OIDC group claim value of 1 to 1024 bytes without control characters.

MemberRoleRequest.description: Gives the grantee exactly this direct role, replacing any other direct role.

MemberRevokeRequest.description: Revokes every direct role of the grantee. Directory-mapped membership is unchanged.

ShareRequest.description: Shares the item with the grantee at exactly this access, replacing another.

ShareRevokeRequest.description: Revokes the grantee's share. The grantee need not remain a project member.

Grantee.description: A grant recipient as recorded. grantee_id is absent for `project`.

ConversationAccess.description: What the caller may do with one item. Items are private to their creator until shared; another user's unshared item is not_found.

project_id.description: The containing project, or null in a personal scope.

access.description: The caller's effective access. Never more than read in an archived project. Open vocabulary.

can_manage_shares.description: The caller may share this item or revoke its shares.

ArtifactAccess.description: What the caller may do with one item. Items are private to their creator until shared; another user's unshared item is not_found.

project_id.description: The containing project, or null in a personal scope.

access.description: The caller's effective access. Never more than read in an archived project. Open vocabulary.

can_manage_shares.description: The caller may share this item or revoke its shares.

Sha256Digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the content in lowercase hexadecimal.

ArtifactUploadMetadata.description: The metadata part of an artifact upload. It has no members yet; new optional members are additive. Unknown members fail with validation.

ArtifactUploadRequest.description: One artifact upload: exactly one file part and one metadata part, in either order. Any other part, a repeated part, a part header other than Content-Disposition and Content-Type, filename*, or a body without its closing delimiter fails with validation. The multipart boundary and the part order are not part of the request identity: a retry may use another boundary and order.

file.description: The file bytes, at most max_bytes. The part needs an explicit Content-Type, which becomes the revision's media_type (not multipart/*); its optional filename, without any directory part, becomes display_name and never a path.

ArtifactRevision.description: One immutable artifact revision. It never carries a storage path or an internal reservation.

revision.description: The revision number: 1 for the first, then consecutive.

project_id.description: The containing project, or null in a personal scope.

media_type.description: The file part's Content-Type as the server normalized it: the type in lower case, then any parameters, separated by semicolons without white space. Served as the download's Content-Type.

display_name.description: The uploaded file name without any directory part, or null. Display metadata only.

state.description: Lifecycle state. Only active revisions serve content; retained, purging and purged do not. Open vocabulary.

Run.description: Consistent run snapshot. A terminal event is null for a live run or a terminal run that predates terminal events. Resume after last_sequence with resume_cursor.

state.description: Open state vocabulary. During reconciliation the wire state is running.

ModelDescriptor.description: An installed catalog descriptor visible under current caller and platform policy. Readiness stays unknown until the provider has a current observation.

PresetDescriptor.description: An installed catalog descriptor visible under current caller and platform policy. Readiness stays unknown until the provider has a current observation.

context_window.description: A positive decimal token count. Project defaults also accept existing integer values.

output_reserve.description: A positive decimal token count. Project defaults also accept existing integer values.

arguments_json.description: Exact canonical UTF-8 JSON text of the reviewed arguments.

CapabilitiesMixed.summary: Independent installed, authorization and readiness dimensions (synthetic, illustrative identifiers)

CapabilitiesCoreOnly.summary: Core installation with no optional provider installed

ApprovalDecision.summary: Submit a decision for the displayed binding
